# OpenTokenUsage

> OpenTokenUsage is a free, open-source (MIT) Windows 11 tray app that shows how much of your AI coding subscriptions you've used: session (5-hour) and weekly limits, credits, reset times and pace, for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, GitHub Copilot and 21 more providers. It also adds up what you spend each day, and for Claude and Codex what each project costs. It is the Windows counterpart of macOS menu bar apps like CodexBar and OpenUsage.

- Platform: Windows 11 only (no macOS or Linux build).
- Install: `winget install PowerUserZ.OpenTokenUsage`, or the setup .exe from GitHub Releases. It installs for the current Windows user only (`%LOCALAPPDATA%\OpenTokenUsage`), so neither the install nor updates ask for admin rights. The installer isn't code-signed: a setup downloaded in a browser gets a SmartScreen warning (More info, then Run anyway); winget and in-app updates don't.
- Updates: the app checks every 15 minutes, downloads a new version and installs it quietly when you click Restart to update.
- Price: free. No account, no telemetry; logins stay on the PC.
- How it works: it reuses the login of each tool you already use (for example Claude Code or the Codex CLI) and asks that provider for your usage. No API keys to paste for Claude or Codex. On first start it turns on the providers it finds you signed in to.
- Providers: Claude (Claude Code's login, or the Claude desktop app's), Codex, GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Antigravity, JetBrains AI Assistant, Devin, Kiro, OpenCode Go, Z.ai, Kimi Code, Kimi API, Factory (Droid), MiniMax, Grok, Amp, Synthetic, Muse Code (off until you turn it on), OpenRouter, DeepSeek, Codebuff, Kilo, Qwen Code, Ollama, and custom balances (New API, One API, Sub2API or your own endpoint).
- Shows: used percent, reset time, pace (ahead or behind an even pace, optionally counting work days only), and when you'll run out at the current rate.
- Spend summary: today, yesterday and the last 30 days in tokens and API-price cost across Claude, Codex and other CLIs' own logs, the models used most, and how many times its price each plan's use was worth.
- Claude and Codex detail pages: usage and cost by project (repository, git branch, ticket key) with monthly budgets and CSV export, the weekly limit by day, usage by weekday and hour, a year of daily use with streaks (kept after Claude Code deletes its logs), prompt cache hit rate, banked rate limit resets with expiry reminders. Their cards list the Claude Code and Codex sessions running on the PC, with context fill and Claude's prompt cache countdown. Costs come from ccusage (needs Bun or Node.js), in one of 13 currencies at a rate you enter.
- Alerts: Windows notifications at chosen usage levels (80% and 95% by default, or per provider), pace warnings and resets, with built-in or custom sounds.
- Tray: app icon, percent (optionally colored by pace), bars, or one number or logo ring per provider; an experimental taskbar strip (on by default) shows session and weekly numbers inside the taskbar, on one monitor or all of them.
- Desktop: widgets with the same providers anywhere on the desktop (side by side, stacked, one per provider or in turn), and a screen-edge rail with today's spend, a usage ring per provider and the live token rate.
- Accounts: a second Claude or Codex account gets its own card, and so does a different login inside a running WSL distro.
- Settings backup: export settings to a file and import them on another PC (logins aren't included).
- Languages: English, German, Spanish (Spain and Latin America), French, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese (Brazil), Turkish, Simplified Chinese.
- Local HTTP API: other apps on the same PC can read usage from 127.0.0.1:6736 (loopback only).
- Network: besides the providers you turn on, the app contacts only their status pages, GitHub for updates, and npm for ccusage.
